knobs.note: Age past which a CI answer is treated as stale.
Whether a refused merge is retried.
Merge retries before the PR is handed off.
Consecutive base holds on one head before one alert (BH-1646).

Read by bin/review-prs.sh as ${MC_MAIN_RED_LABEL:-fix-main-red}, and registered only so that read is visible (section 7 of tests/lanes-registry-test.sh). NOT settable here (BH-1985): the label is set in ONE place, the lib row lib.main-red-label.mc_main_red_label (BH-1770), which every reader resolves first. A lane row would split the label for this lane alone, so lane-gate ignores one; MAIN_RED_LABEL is a deprecated alias.
Reviews in flight for one project before a new one waits. A crashed review is owed exactly one retry.

0 makes this lane call no model at all. bin/lib/llm-gate.sh refuses BEFORE the vendor call and writes a zero-cost row_source=refused row, so the stop is visible in the ledger rather than being a lane that went quiet.

Comma/space list of the ONLY ladder rungs this lane may reach. Empty is every rung, i.e. today's ladder unchanged. A rung outside the list is refused before the call, so a cliff or a failure on the standing lane cannot descend into one that costs ~100x (#1141, the $793 descent).

Dollars this lane may spend in the current UTC day, summed from D1 cost_rows through GET /api/metrics/llm-spend — never from the box's own logs/cost.csv. A second, project-scoped ceiling is the lane.<id>.<project>.llm_usd_cap_day row, which is read only when somebody wrote it.
Consecutive refused dismissals of one standing review before an ALERTS line.

Read by bin/review-prs.sh as ${BASE_BRANCH:-main}: the only base the direct merge lands on (BH-1285); a stacked PR is held. NOT settable from the control plane — it is a repo fact the box env carries, so only env/global.env on the box moves it; the same knob bin/rebase-train.sh registers.

BH-1794: the reviewer prompt carries what GitHub reports for the head under review (each run's name, conclusion and URL, read on this lane's credential ladder; unreadable is said, never red), so a reviewer whose token cannot read check-runs is not left judging CI from a stale PR-body Evidence block. 0 = the prompt is what it was before.

BH-1794: a head this lane already answered REQUEST_CHANGES is reviewed ONCE more when its PR body carries `<!-- harness:rereview-requested <that sha> -->`, which bin/blocked-resolver.sh's fix-round preflight writes when the only blocker was stale evidence and CI is green. Once per head (rereq_sha); the body is read only for a blocked head. 0 = the marker is ignored.

BH-2457: hours one D1-unreadable outage holds paid reviews before the lane reviews on this box's subscription runners only (metered stays refused). 0 turns the fallback off: the lane holds until D1 answers. A value that is not a 0-168 hour count is read as the default.

BH-5284: Builder reviews one tick runs at once (bin/lib/review-pool.sh), each in its own worker with its own claim, heartbeat and scratch dir. 0 = no cap: every eligible review starts, bounded only by the box guardrails, the spend cap and the start cap. Capped per box by REVIEW_BOX_MAX.

BH-5284, BH-5337: a hard cap on REVIEW_CONCURRENCY on this box; it overrides the derived cap. 0 derives one from three terms and the smallest wins: cpu (vCPUs / REVIEW_WORKER_CPUS), memory (MemAvailable / REVIEW_WORKER_MEM_MB; with a tmpfs /tmp, (MemAvailable - tmpfs used) / (REVIEW_WORKER_MEM_MB + REVIEW_WORKER_TMP_MB)) and tmp ((free /tmp - REVIEW_TMP_MIN_MB) / REVIEW_WORKER_TMP_MB, 256 a worker). The tick logs `concurrency capped at N by cpu|memory|tmp (...)`.
BH-5284: no new review worker starts while /tmp has less free space than this; one alert line per low episode. A full /tmp broke lead reviews on 2026-10-06.

BH-5337: vCPUs one builder review worker is given when the box cap is derived (REVIEW_BOX_MAX=0). The cpu term is vCPUs / this, so at 1 a 4 vCPU box runs at most 4 workers whatever its RAM. Ten workers on a 4 vCPU box froze box-small on 2026-10-08.

BH-5337: memory one builder review worker is given when the box cap is derived (REVIEW_BOX_MAX=0): the claude CLI, its checkout and its test run. The memory term is MemAvailable / this; with a tmpfs /tmp the tmpfs use comes off MemAvailable and REVIEW_WORKER_TMP_MB is added to this. Was 1024 in code before BH-5337.
BH-6132: the /tmp space one review worker needs. rpool_init sizes the /tmp cap as (free - REVIEW_TMP_MIN_MB) / this; the review-prs-tmp-capped event reports it as worker_tmp_mb.

BH-5284: after an agent call hits a rate or concurrency limit (429, overloaded, the account's concurrency cap) no new review starts for this long; it doubles on each repeat up to 900s and resets on the next review that ends normally. The limited review records no verdict and is not counted as failed.

BH-6130, BH-6133: a review pool capped below 3 by /tmp sends its Sentry event (free space, threshold, the count of review-prs dirs, the three largest /tmp entries) once per cap episode, and again each window while the episode lasts, plus once when the cap drops below the last reported value (BH-6132). An episode ends when a tick measures free /tmp at or above TMP_MIN_MB + 3 x WORKER_TMP_MB. 0 turns the window off: every capped tick reports, under the Sentry lib's own per-hour cap. The marker state/review-prs-tmp-capped.last is shared by every project on the box.
